harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s legacy SQLite reservation utility. Concurrent requests are serialized, successful IDs are idempotent, stock cannot become negative, invalid or insufficient requests are rejected, and lock waits terminate after five seconds. Existing data survived the repair and node restart.
actions_performed: Updated bin/reserve.py using Python 2.5/SQLite 3.4.2-compatible transaction handling.
Stress-tested competing requests and duplicate request IDs.
Safely restarted node1 and confirmed persistence with an unchanged kernel.

evidence.requirement: Concurrent requests decrement stock exactly once and never below zero
evidence.summary: From stock 10, 20 concurrent requests produced exactly 10 successes and 10 insufficient-stock rejections; remaining stock was 0 with no negative rows.
Eight concurrent calls using one ID returned the same result while creating one row and one decrement. The preserved previous-request also returned its stored quantity without changing live data.

evidence.requirement: Reject invalid quantities and insufficient stock while preserving reservations
evidence.summary: Zero quantity and insufficient stock were rejected; database integrity was OK, stock remained 5, and previous-request=2 remained the sole reservation.
Under a held write lock, the request exited after five seconds with 'database is locked' and made no data change.

evidence.requirement: Remain compatible with the installed legacy operating system and kernel
evidence.summary: Repair uses the installed Ubuntu 7.10, Python 2.5.1, and SQLite 3.4.2 environment; kernel remained 2.6.22-14-generic across restart.

Healthy baseline boot ID bdfe94ce-858d-4667-8a5e-b8be63a7aafd was captured, restart was acknowledged, new boot ID e6042f6f-99cb-421a-b2a7-25db6af8d5fe was observed, and the executable, checksum, database integrity, preserved data, idempotency, and rejection behavior recovered successfully.
